title: Processing human lymph node samples for single-cell assays
protocol: Transfer lymph node into a sterile mortar and add 5 mL cell culture medium.
Remove excessive fat and connective tissue using dissecting scissors or a scalpel.
Cut lymph node into small pieces of approximately 1–2 mm size using dissecting scissors and forceps.
Thoroughly pipette up and down using a 5 mL serological pipette to gently wash out the lymphocytes from the lymph node pieces.
Filter lymphocyte-containing medium through a 100 μm strainer into a sterile 50 mL tube.
Add 5 ml cell culture medium and repeat washing steps once or twice depending on the size of the lymph node.
Centrifuge the tube at 400 g for 5 min at 18°C–25°C.
Carefully decant the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 10 ml cell culture medium and pass through a 70 μm strainer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 18°C–25°C.
Resuspend cells in cell culture medium.
Count cells and set aside 1 × 10^6 cells for quality control by flow cytometry.
Dilute cell suspensions to a desired cell concentration using cell culture medium, such as 5 × 10^6 cells per 700 μL medium.
Fill 2 mL cryotubes with 700 μL of cold freezing medium.
Add 700 μL of diluted cell suspension drop-wise to the cryotubes and gently invert tubes a few times.
Place cryotubes quickly into a slow freezing container.
Store cryotubes at -80°C for ≥ 24 hours.
Long-term storage should be below -150°C.
Transfer 1 × 10^6 cells into a 5 mL flow cytometry tube.
Add 1 mL of washing buffer to the cells.
Centrifuge the cells at 400 g for 5 minutes at 18°C–25°C.
Decant and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 50-100 μL of remaining buffer.
Add antibodies as shown in Table 1.
Briefly vortex the mixture.
Incubate at 4°C protected from light for 30 minutes.
Add 1 mL of washing buffer to the cells.
Centrifuge the cells at 400 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat for a total of three washes.
Resuspend cells in 200 μL washing buffer.
Put cells on ice and analyze them on a flow cytometer within 24 h.
Pre-warm water bath and EDTA-containing cell culture medium to 37°C.
Prepare 50 mL tubes with 10 mL of EDTA-containing cell culture medium.
Thaw frozen aliquots in pre-warmed water bath.
Transfer cell suspension dropwise into prepared tubes.
Centrifuge cells at 200 g for 5 min at 18°C–25°C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in EDTA-free washing buffer.
Filter cell suspensions through 75 μm strainer.
Count cells manually using trypan blue and a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge cells at 200 g for 5 min at 18°C–25°C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL magnetic beads per 1 × 10^7 cells.
Incubate for 15 min protected from light at 18°C–25°C.
Wash each column with 500 μL 1X binding buffer.
Wait until the liquid has passed the column and place a tissue beneath to soak up the flow-through.
Place 15 mL tubes under each column to collect the flow-through.
Add 1 mL 1X binding buffer to each sample and apply onto one column.
Wait until the liquid has passed the column before rinsing with 500 μL 1X binding buffer.
Perform a total of 4 washes in this way.
Centrifuge the collected flow-through at 200 g for 5 min at 18°C–25°C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in washing buffer and handle them at 4°C from here on.
Count cells and assess viability using trypan blue and a hemocytometer.
Evaluate continuation of the protocol if cell viability does not exceed 85% in any sample.
Thaw an additional vial of cells as back-up when viability is unexpectedly low.
Expect to recover only a median of 3.5 × 10^6 viable cells from a vial containing 1 × 10^7 total cells.
Optimize conditions for cell recovery and viability based on troubleshooting guidelines if necessary.
Optional: Label cells with barcoded antibodies at this step, but do not stain before removing dead cells.
Continue with library preparation for single-cell sequencing according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
